name: Partition Permutation Distribution
miniText: Does randomly building an integer total sample its mathematical partitions uniformly? NetLogo Partition Permutation Distribution repeatedly draws positive addends, retaining those that fit until the target sum is reached, then accumulates addend frequencies. A switch changes whether candidate values come from the remaining gap or the original range. Andrews [1] defines integer partitions, Hardy and Ramanujan [2] develop partition-count asymptotics, and Durrett [3] supplies the probability framework for analyzing the actual sampling procedure. These sources expose a crucial distinction: the baseline generates ordered construction histories with unequal probabilities, rather than enumerating unordered partitions uniformly. Histogram shape therefore reflects the stochastic algorithm as well as arithmetic constraints. The model illustrates how a shrinking sample space changes observed frequencies; it does not estimate the partition function merely by plotting successful addends.
